projects.title: Retrieved But Not Reliable
projects.subtitle: Mapping attacks and defenses across the RAG pipeline
projects.paper_title: Retrieved But Not Reliable: A Survey on Attacks, and Defenses in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
projects.summary: A pipeline-aware view of how retrieval-augmented systems fail, and where defenses can intervene.
projects.abstract: Retrieval can ground an answer in external knowledge while also exposing new ways to manipulate it. This survey organizes RAG attacks by their effects on accuracy, privacy, and fairness, and maps defenses to retrieval, reranking, generation, and traceback. By bringing threat models, evaluation benchmarks, and explainability methods into one framework, the work helps researchers identify vulnerable stages and assess defenses across the full retrieval-augmented pipeline.
projects.contribution: Conducted a pipeline-aware survey of RAG robustness and security, organizing threat models, attacks, defenses, benchmarks, and explainability methods.
projects.authors: Minh Tran, Cuong Dang, Tuc Nguyen, Khanh-Tung Tran, Minh Huynh Nguyen, Trinh Chau, Kien Le, Do Xuan Long, Jiahao Zhang, Fali Wang, Hoang D. Nguyen, Thanh Le, Suhang Wang
projects.image_alt: Original paper overview showing RAG attack surfaces and defense strategies around the database, retriever, reranker, and generator.

projects.title: URAG
projects.subtitle: Measuring uncertainty in retrieval-augmented LLMs
projects.paper_title: URAG: A Benchmark for Uncertainty Quantification in Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models
projects.summary: Looking beyond answer accuracy to ask when a retrieval-augmented model should be uncertain.
projects.abstract: A correct answer alone does not explain whether a retrieval-augmented model is reliable. URAG evaluates accuracy alongside uncertainty across eight datasets spanning five domains. Its construction pipeline turns open-ended tasks into multiple-choice questions with challenging distractors, enabling conformal prediction to measure uncertainty through prediction sets. The benchmark examines how retrieval noise, retrieval depth, and a model's existing knowledge affect confidence, revealing settings where additional evidence can still lead to overconfident errors.
projects.contribution: Contributed to the benchmark and developed a standardized pipeline for converting open-ended RAG tasks into multiple-choice questions for uncertainty assessment.
projects.authors: Vinh Nguyen*, Cuong Dang*, Jiahao Zhang, Hoa Tran, Minh Tran, Trinh Chau, Thai Le, Lu Cheng, Suhang Wang. *Equal contribution.

projects.title: VialectBench
projects.subtitle: Testing LLMs across Vietnamese dialects
projects.paper_title: How Robust Are LLMs to Vietnamese Dialects?
projects.summary: A controlled benchmark for whether model decisions stay consistent across regional Vietnamese.
projects.abstract: Meaning can stay the same even when regional language changes. VialectBench tests whether LLM predictions remain stable across six Vietnamese dialect groups, using 400 standard-language instances and 2,400 human-written rewrites across four language-understanding tasks. Evaluation of ten instruction-tuned models measures performance loss, prediction inconsistency, and harmful answer flips. The study shows that strong results on standard Vietnamese can conceal failures on regional variants, motivating more representative evaluation of Vietnamese language technologies.
projects.contribution: Introduced VialectBench and evaluated instruction-tuned LLMs for dialect-induced performance degradation, inconsistent predictions, and harmful answer flips.
projects.authors: Minh Tran*, Trinh Chau*, Thanh-Nhan Le, Nam Tran, Luan Thanh Nguyen, Cuong Dang, Duc Hoang. *Equal contribution.

projects.title: EVENTA
projects.subtitle: Finding images through the events they capture
projects.paper_title: A Hybrid Dense-Sparse Multi-Stage Re-ranking Framework for Event-Based Image Retrieval
projects.summary: Hybrid retrieval connects natural-language event descriptions with relevant images and article context.
projects.abstract: Event descriptions often require more context than a visual match alone can provide. This system combines OpenCLIP image-text embeddings with Nomic semantic retrieval and BM25 lexical search. Reciprocal Rank Fusion merges the retrieval signals, while semantic chunking and multiple reranking stages refine article and image relevance. Developed for the EVENTA challenge, the project received second prize and the team presented its approach at an ACM Multimedia workshop.
projects.contribution: Engineered a two-phase retrieval system with offline embeddings and semantic chunking, followed by online dense–sparse fusion and multi-stage reranking.
projects.authors: Team project. The public challenge manuscript is anonymized; the project association and award are documented in the supplied CV.

projects.title: AI Assistant Glasses
projects.subtitle: Anticipating hazards for accessible mobility
projects.summary: Smart glasses combine audio and visual signals to alert visually impaired users to nearby dangers.
projects.abstract: Assistive systems need to recognize how a scene may change as well as what it contains. This smart-glasses project combines audio and visual information to provide danger alerts for visually impaired users. An LSTM component predicts future states of moving objects, supporting alerts about evolving hazards. The project won the HCMUS × Bosch AI Innovation Competition 2024 and explores the use of computer vision and temporal modeling for accessible mobility.
projects.contribution: Built multimodal danger-alert functionality and implemented an LSTM to predict future states of moving objects.

projects.title: Flood Forecasting for the Long Dai River
projects.subtitle: Hydrologic machine learning for Central Vietnam
projects.summary: Guiding students from hydrologic data to a seven-day flood forecasting prototype for a Vietnamese river.
projects.abstract: Flood forecasting connects machine learning with a pressing local challenge in Central Vietnam. As a SEAS project mentor, I guided students developing a prototype for forecasting discharge in the Long Dai River up to seven days ahead. The project used filtered U.S. CAMELS hydrologic data and Open-Meteo inputs, with comparison against Google Flood Hub. Mentorship focused on connecting data selection and model development to the practical challenges of applying a forecasting system in Vietnam.
projects.contribution: Mentored the student team's project design and development as part of Summer in Engineering and Applied Sciences. This is a student prototype; the CV does not report operational deployment or validated forecast accuracy.

projects.title: Local Fish Recognition at the Edge
projects.subtitle: Computer vision for Dong Hoi's marine species
projects.summary: Mentoring a student team exploring efficient fish-species classification on resource-constrained devices.
projects.abstract: Recognizing local fish species can support marine biodiversity education and ecosystem monitoring. At SEAS, I mentored a student team developing a computer-vision system for fish native to Dong Hoi, Quang Binh. Using FishNet as a data resource, the project explored efficient classification and edge-deployment techniques for resource-constrained hardware. Students connected dataset preparation and model development with the practical constraints of real-time recognition in a locally relevant application.
projects.contribution: Mentored the student team's design of an edge-oriented fish identification application. Real-time operation and hardware deployment are project objectives; the public repository does not report measured speed or deployment results.
